subject: Follow-up: modeling effective $/1M tokens with prefix caching (post-demo)
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morris <kate@finclient.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, May 15, 2026 at 4:22 PM PDT
Subject: Follow-up: modeling effective $/1M tokens with prefix caching (post-demo)

Kate — great to speak today. Quick recap and the lightweight model we discussed so you can see how caching changes the effective unit economics. Please confirm the two main inputs from your side (monthly token volume and target effective $/1M) and we can iterate the attached spreadsheet.

Key inputs I used (assumptions, please adjust):
- Baseline list price used for modeling: $1,000 per 1M tokens (this is the illustrative model price for the workload class we discussed).
- Typical request: ~200 generated tokens on average.
- Prefix reuse: many of your flows reuse a short system prompt + user template (~40 tokens). We model hits only when the full prefix is cached.
- Prefix cache hit rate (variable below).

Simple conversion (how to read the numbers):
- Effective_spend_per_1M = list_price * (1 - hit_rate)
- Example values:
  - hit_rate 20% -> effective $/1M = $800
  - hit_rate 40% -> effective $/1M = $600
  - hit_rate 60% -> effective $/1M = $400

Why this matters: if you can get to a ~40–50% prefix hit on your most common flows, the effective spend on generation drops materially and lets you hit tighter budget targets (or move to a higher-capacity model for the same spend).

Open questions I flagged for Marissa/Dev to validate with your engineers:
1) What percent of calls are templated vs. free-form? We modeled 65% templated; if templated is higher, hit rates should improve.
2) Typical prefix lengths and whether prefixes vary by user locale or customer segment.
3) Do you use session-level memory that would increase KV cache reuse (we assumed no persistent per-user KV beyond a short session).

Next steps proposed:
- Kate and Tom: confirm monthly token volume estimate and target effective $/1M.
- Marissa: technical deep-dive to validate prefix distributions (30–45 min).
- I attached a starter spreadsheet (prefix_cache_model_v1.xlsx) with the scenarios; I'll upload a read-only copy to the Drive link below.

Attachments: prefix_cache_model_v1.xlsx (attachment), redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (attachment)

Thanks — talk soon,

Subject: Re: Follow-up: modeling effective $/1M tokens with prefix caching (post-demo)

Thanks, Sergio — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Monthly blended token estimate (current + projected growth): 150,000,000 tokens/month (rough).
- Our procurement target: effective $/1M in the neighborhood of $450–$550 (goal: $500).
- Templated flows: around 70% of requests follow our canned prompts (support responses, onboarding flows).
- Average generation length is closer to 180 tokens, prefix ~35 tokens.
- We do maintain short-lived session memory (per-login session, typically cleared after inactivity) — not persistent cross-session today.

Can you run the attached model with a 45% hit-rate baseline and show a conservative + optimistic scenario (+/- 10 percentage points)? Also please call out any trade-offs if we wanted to prioritize higher hit rates (e.g., longer prefix normalization, additional prefetching, prompt engineering).

Tom and I are available Tue afternoon for the technical call.

—Kate

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, May 16, 2026 at 18:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Follow-up: modeling effective $/1M tokens with prefix caching (post-demo)

Appreciate the detail, Kate — that helps a lot. I've updated the scenario in the spreadsheet and included three rows you can reference: conservative (35% hit), baseline (45% hit), optimistic (55% hit). Quick numbers (using list price $1,000/1M):
- 35% hit -> effective $/1M = $650
- 45% hit -> effective $/1M = $550
- 55% hit -> effective $/1M = $450

At 150M tokens/month, that maps to monthly spend (illustrative):
- 35% hit -> $97,500/month
- 45% hit -> $82,500/month
- 55% hit -> $67,500/month

Notes on levers to improve hit rate (high level):
- Prompt normalization: canonicalize variable fields (user names, timestamps) to increase prefix matches. Engineering effort: small but requires coordination with product templates.
- Shorter normalized prefixes: focus on the first 30–50 tokens as the caching key for most flows; reduces variability but may miss some phenotype-specific cues.
- Prefetch/batch: for multi-step flows, prefetching likely hits the cache more often; adds some latency/risk trade-offs for user-facing flows.
- Session KV: if you can safely persist small session keys for the lifetime of a session, reuse increases without changing prompts.

Marissa/Dev — can you validate the modeling assumptions (avg gen length 180, prefix 35, templated% 70) and confirm whether Redwood's continuous batching and prefix caching behave as assumed (cache matches full-prefix only)?

I propose we meet Tue 2026-05-19 at 2:30 PM PT for a short tech session. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and Marissa will bring a short checklist (what logs/metrics we need to estimate hit rate from your traffic).

Sergio

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: modeling effective $/1M tokens with prefix caching (post-demo)

Kate — thanks for the availability. Quick tech prep notes before Tue: what would be most useful for us to estimate a real hit-rate from your traffic (we can do this from a small pulled sample):
- 48–72 hours of anonymized request logs (timestamp, prompt hash, prompt length, generated length). If you can't export prompt text, a stable hash is fine.
- Breakdown by route (support bot, onboarding, search summarization) — templated flows often live in specific routes.
- Any rate limits or batching constraints in your client that might alter request patterns.

I'll also attach the CSV export template in Drive and run a quick local analysis during our call to give you a data-backed hit-rate estimate. If the 45% baseline holds, Sergio's pricing scenarios hit your $500 target (baseline). If it's materially lower, we'll sketch an engineering roadmap and estimated uplift to get you there.
